title: When a Houston Roof Needs a Permit
description: A full roof replacement in the City of Houston is a permitted job. A few-shingle repair is not the same thing, and the suburbs do not share one counter.
html:
The question is not whether roofing is “city business.” The question is which desk the house sits under, and whether the job is a replacement or a patch. Those two answers change the permit, the inspection, and what a low bid is quietly skipping.

Replacement and repair are not the same filing

Inside the City of Houston, plan on a permit for a tear-off and replacement. A repair of a few courses, a pipe boot, or a flashing detail is a different conversation, and we do not dress a repair up as a replacement to avoid the paperwork or the other way around. The permit is pulled before the shingles come off, in the name of the company doing the work, not left as a homeowner errand on the morning of the job.

The suburbs do not share Houston’s counter. Tomball, Katy, Sugar Land, Cypress, The Woodlands, and unincorporated Harris County each have their own rules. A house with a Houston mailing address can still sit in the county. We look up the jurisdiction for that address. A bid that says “no permit needed” on a full replacement, without naming the city, is a bid to read twice.

What the inspection is for

Where the city inspects, the point is the deck, the underlayment, and the details, not a drive-by of the finished color. Some places want a look while the deck is open. Some want a final. We schedule around that so a crew is not shingling a roof the inspector still needs to see. The permit card is not a decoration for the window. It is the record that the job was allowed.

Permits do not make a roof good. A permitted roof can still be a thin underlayment and a rushed valley. An unpermitted replacement can look fine until you sell, refinance, or file a claim and someone asks for the record. On a roof replacement we include the permit for the jurisdiction you are actually in, and the scope says so in writing. If you are comparing bids, ask who pulls it and when. Call (281) 541-0027 or request the inspection and we will tell you which counter your address uses.
